package_info.package_manager: N/A (JavaScript library, distributed via npm, CDN, or bundled in CMSes)
package_info.why_malicious: CKEditor 4 versions prior to 4.16.1 contain a stored XSS vulnerability (CVE-2021-33829) due to improper sanitization of HTML comments containing the reserved 'cke_protected' keyword. Attackers can inject specially crafted payloads that bypass the intended protection, resulting in arbitrary script execution in the context of users editing content.

execution_context.file_location: rich text content field (e.g., blog post, CMS page, admin editor)
required_permissions: none (attacker needs ability to submit content)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views or edits the content, the injected tag executes JavaScript via the onerror handler, resulting in XSS.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The payload leverages malformed HTML comments and the reserved 'cke_protected' keyword to bypass sanitization and inject executable JavaScript.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: User-supplied HTML should be sanitized to prevent script execution; instead, the protection is bypassed, allowing XSS.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of HTML comments and tags, but not with event handlers for code execution.
key_indicators: Use of reserved 'cke_protected' keyword in user content
Inline JavaScript event handler (onerror) in tag

execution_context.file_location: rich text content field (e.g., blog post, CMS page, admin editor)
required_permissions: none (attacker needs ability to submit content)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views or edits the content, the nested 'cke_protected' keyword bypasses single-pass sanitization, resulting in the tag executing JavaScript via the onerror handler.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The payload exploits recursive/nested use of the reserved keyword to evade the single-pass removal logic, enabling XSS.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Sanitization should recursively remove or encode all protected keywords, but the implementation only removes one layer.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; nested reserved keywords are not expected in legitimate content.

execution_context.file_location: rich text content field (e.g., blog post, CMS page, admin editor)
required_permissions: none (attacker needs ability to submit content)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views or edits the content, the payload with a doubly-nested reserved keyword and malformed comment closure bypasses sanitization, resulting in XSS via the tag.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The payload demonstrates that the sanitization logic fails to handle multiple or malformed nested reserved keywords, allowing script injection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Sanitization should handle all forms of reserved keyword injection, but fails with complex nesting.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; such complex nesting is not legitimate.

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits specially crafted HTML payload containing reserved 'cke_protected' keyword and malformed HTML comments to a CKEditor 4 instance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is stored in the application database or content field.

attack_chain.action: Another user (or the attacker) opens the vulnerable content in CKEditor 4 in edit mode.
attack_chain.leads_to: CKEditor 4 processes the content, fails to sanitize the payload, and renders the malicious tag.

attack_chain.action: The browser interprets the malformed comment, exposes the tag, and executes the onerror JavaScript handler.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary JavaScript executes in the victim's browser (XSS), leading to account takeover, credential theft, or further attacks.

behavioral_signatures: User-supplied content containing the 'cke_protected' keyword in HTML comments
Malformed HTML comments (e.g., --!> instead of -->) in user content
Presence of tags with inline JavaScript event handlers (e.g., onerror) in stored content
file_indicators: Rich text fields or database entries containing <!--{cke_protected}--!> or nested variants
network_indicators: N/A (XSS is a client-side attack; network indicators may only appear if exfiltration is attempted by the payload)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan user-submitted or stored HTML content for the presence of the 'cke_protected' keyword within HTML comments, especially with malformed comment closures (e.g., --!>). Flag any content containing tags with inline event handlers such as onerror. Monitor for attempts to inject or render such payloads in CKEditor 4 instances, and alert on any execution of suspicious JavaScript in the context of the editor.
